concepts.outside: Create one finished landscape 3:2 environment concept painting for a realistic historical central-European village game. Eye level at an open timber yard gate in the village interior approaching from the north-east, looking across an elongated compact working stable forecourt to a SINGLE one-storey long stable along the distant south stone curtain wall, its eave side facing us. About 22m long and 8m deep, low steep irregular dark slate roof, five equal-looking bays in a warm weathered oak frame with big pegged knee braces, pale limewashed rubble-stone infill on low stone footings. Four 1.5m wide upper-open Dutch half doors on the sunny yard eave, fifth right/east bay is an open fodder unloading bay. A generous continuous unobstructed earth path down the length of the eave turns into the L-shaped forecourt at front right, worn pair of broad wheel tracks in tamped ochre earth. A shallow monolithic limestone drinking trough and a weathered hitch beam are tucked well to the side by rail fence, dull forged rings, golden straw visible only at stall thresholds. Clean clear open central yard that can turn a cart. A horse at far left for scale, if helpful. Quiet morning after rain, zinc-grey sky, warm amber bounce from worn timber, a glimpse of trees above the crenellated fieldstone south wall behind, the roof gable and the wall are separate with a service strip. Authentic central European medieval village carpentry. Distinct story from rubbed door edges, repair patches and iron hardware. Beautiful considered composition, textured restrained digital gouache mixed with architectural realism, eye for real construction and use, tactile materials, editorial environment development plate. No titles, no lettering, no watermark, no heavy vignette, no fantasy ornaments, no Victorian machinery. It is a village amenity, all the conveyed activity is agricultural and peaceful.
concepts.inside: Create one finished landscape 3:2 game environment interior concept, part of the same central-European hillside village stable design: long one-storey 22m x 8m fieldstone-and-weathered-oak stable, 5 bays high exposed pegged oak pitched trusses, uneven grey slate roof outside. Camera inside its eastern fodder bay looking WEST down a real uninterrupted 2.4m wide lengthwise service aisle at the REAR (south) of the building. On the RIGHT (north) are four horse boxes with oak plank partitions below shoulder level, simple ironwork and tie rings, feeding rack, a glimpse of horses and amber daylight from upper-open split Dutch doors to their exterior court. On the LEFT is a continuous pale limewashed rear masonry wall, a few high narrow vents, period joinery and practical storage confined to alcoves. Gathering straw, packed clay floor, timber grain burnished by use, iron strap on an oak half door, sunlight painting irregular soft pools on weathered planks. Grounded late medieval Bohemia agrarian architecture. Human scale, believable construction. Painterly realism, gouache and sophisticated material study, muted slate and straw palette, warm daylight, readable midtones. Single intentional shot; no lettering or labels, no split panels, no modern equestrian metal cages, no anachronisms. It is a peaceful rural stable.
